newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stevedores to hold extra talks with Cosipa.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stevedores to hold extra talks with Cosipa.

text.p: Brazilian stevedores will hold fresh talks with steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) Thursday but could start a new strike at Santos port in May if the negotiations fail, an official said.
A first round of talks Tuesday was aimed at resolving a labor dispute which has already triggered two strikes at Santos as well as two national port stoppages.

Union representatives, in a meeting with Cosipa officials earlier, proposed reducing the size of work teams and the amount of overtime pay but did not receive an immediate reply from the steel company.
"We ceded a 40 percent reduction in the size of our teams," said Orlando Santana, treasurer of the Santos Stevedores' Union. "The company said it would give us a reply on Thursday."
Fresh talks were scheduled for 1400 local/1700 GMT local on April 24, he added.
The stevedores have held strikes and occupied vessels at Cosipa's private terminal at Santos port in protest against the company's decision to use its own workers to load and unload vessels.
Under a temporary agreement struck last Friday, they agreed to share the operation of vessels at the Cosipa terminal with the company's own staff on a 50-50 basis.
But this was a strictly temporary measure which would end on April 30, union officials said, adding that if no permament solution had been found by then, there could be a fresh strike.
"It could be," said Santana when asked if another strike was likely on May 1.
"In the beginning it would be regional, and then we would have to see if other ports want to join in."

He said the stevedores had also proposed reducing the number of work hours considered extraordinary, such as lunchtime, although those working on Sundays and holidays would still be eligible for overtime pay.

Separate from the talks, several union representatives were in the capital Brasilia to try to push through a bill by Deputy Vicente Cascione to reintegrate the private terminals of Cosipa and another firm, Ultravertil, into the port structure.
Officials from Santos earlier this month met the president of the lower house of Congress Michel Temer to discuss the bill.
